$ python -c "import sqlparse; print(sqlparse.parse('SELECT 1')[0]); print(sqlparse.parse('SELECT a, b FROM foo ORDER BY a, b')[0]); print(sqlparse.parse('x := 1')[0]); print(sqlparse.parse('SELECT 1 AS foo')[0])"
status: success; exit code: 0; 92 ms
--- stdout ---
SELECT 1
SELECT a, b FROM foo ORDER BY a, b
x := 1
SELECT 1 AS foo

The regression was in sqlparse/utils.py's imt() helper: it now dereferences token.ttype without first checking for None, whereas many call sites in grouping.py pass tokens that can legitimately be None (e.g. results of token_next/token_prev at the boundaries of a token list, or an absent nidx). This causes `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'ttype'` for statements where such boundary conditions arise (invalid/incomplete identifiers, trailing ORDER BY clauses, `AS` at the end of a statement, etc.) - matching the reported symptoms ('grouping identifier invalid', 'issue284 as grouping', 8 'parse order' cases, and one more).

Fix applied: added an early `if token is None: return False` guard at the top of `imt()` in sqlparse/utils.py, restoring the previous safe behavior (None token -> no match) instead of raising.

Verified with a few manual sanity checks (basic SELECT, ORDER BY with identifier list, assignment `:=`, `AS` aliasing) — all parse without error and produce sensible groupings. No tests directory was present in this checkout to run the hidden test suite directly, but the fix directly addresses the reported AttributeError and is a minimal, targeted change that shouldn't affect any currently-passing behavior (previously `imt` would only be called with non-None tokens in the paths that worked, so the new guard is purely additive safety).

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.
